messages:
Alex C: Hey — quick one. I ran a few nsys + perfetto captures on the KV-cache regression. Where should I upload the raw traces (nsys, perfetto, nvprof) so infra/reviewers can grab them? Also what exactly do we need to redact before sharing internally — there might be customer prompt snippets in the KV cache.

Maria S: s3 is fine: s3://redwood-perf/traces/eng-runtime/ is our canonical spot for perf traces. If file > 10GB use multipart or put in perf-temp and tell infra to move it. For one-off sharing you can also use an internal presigned link. :white_check_mark:

Sam R: +1 to the bucket. What do we scrub from the KV cache? Is it okay to leave token hashes/IDs? 

Jordan L: KV cache can contain raw user tokens (literally input text) depending on how you captured it. Must scrub any user content, email/phone/ip, and anything that looks like API keys. We treat token-level context as PII for shared traces.

Maria S: Here's the minimal checklist we expect before upload: 
- run the scrub tool (tools/perf_scrub.py) to remove text payloads
- include metadata.json next to the trace (see example below)
- follow naming convention so reviewers know model/commit/kvcache state

PerfBot: Automated reminder: attach metadata.json with keys [model, commit_sha, seq_len_dist, kv_cache_state, batch_config, hw_desc]. Missing metadata slows triage.

Alex C: Can someone post the naming convention & metadata example? I'll scrub and upload. :eyes:

Taylor P: Naming convention we use now: <team>-<model>-<desc>-<kvstate>-YYYYMMDD-<shortsha>.nsys (example: engruntime-gptj-ckpt1-kv-warm-20260318-3b7f2a.nsight). Put perf artifacts under a subdir by date and issue: s3://redwood-perf/traces/eng-runtime/2026-03-18/

Jordan L: Metadata example (put as metadata.json next to the upload):
```
model: gptj-8b
commit_sha: 7f2a3b1
kv_cache_state: warm
seq_len_dist: "[8:0.12, 64:0.6, 256:0.28]"
batch_config: "max_batch=32, max_latency_ms=50, continuous_batching=true"
hw_desc: a40x2
note: short description of the failing scenario + any steps to reproduce
```

Sam R: For scrubbing we have a script: `python tools/perf_scrub.py --input trace.nsight --output trace.scrub.nsight --redact-rules redaction.yaml`. redaction.yaml includes regexes for emails, ip addresses, and a rule to zero-out KV payloads. Use `--dry-run` first to see hits.

Alex C: Good — one more: Kernel timelines and raw kernel names (cuLaunch/KERNEL) — do we keep those? We need them for hotspot analysis.

Maria S: Keep kernel timelines, kernel names, and timings. Do NOT keep any attached args that contain raw text or file paths pointing to customer buckets. If in doubt, scrub paths to `/customer-data/` -> `/scrubbed/`.

PerfBot: If you upload, please include a short manifest in the PR or ticket with: S3 path, file sizes, scrub tool output (hits), and who to ping for follow-up.

Jordan L: For huge bundles (>50GB) prefer attaching a small repro trace (1-2 min) + full trace on s3 + a short perf profile (top kernels + counts). That speeds initial triage.

Taylor P: TL;DR checklist: run scrub, attach metadata.json, follow naming, upload to s3://redwood-perf/traces/eng-runtime/YYYY-MM-DD/, paste link in the ticket, and @eng-runtime/oncall if you need help. :lock:

Alex C: Awesome — I'll scrub and upload now. Will ping when done. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
